content:
Samuel Achterberg-Osei
Cloud Infrastructure / Platform Engineer

Contact
Email: [EMAIL]
Phone: [PHONE]

Professional Summary
Cloud infrastructure engineer with experience designing, building and operating Azure environments. Hands-on experience with Terraform, Azure DevOps pipelines, AKS operations, cloud networking and PowerShell automation. Led a 60-server VMware-to-Azure migration completed over six weekends with no unplanned downtime. Experienced in making internal application deployments more frequent through automated build, test and deployment pipelines.

Technical Skills
Cloud and infrastructure: Microsoft Azure, Azure IaaS, Azure Migrate, Azure landing zones, Azure VMs
Infrastructure as code and automation: Terraform, Terraform modules, PowerShell; Python (small scripts); Go (Terratest tests)
CI/CD and containers: Azure DevOps YAML Pipelines, Docker, Helm, AKS, App Service
Networking and security: Hub-spoke networking, VNets, VNet peering, Azure Firewall, private DNS zones, private endpoints, site-to-site VPN, Microsoft 365 security baseline, Entra ID
Systems: Windows and Linux servers, VMware, Proxmox homelab

Professional Experience

Cloud Engineer (Contract) | Havenstad Logistics | 2025–Present
- Build and maintain Azure landing-zone infrastructure, Terraform modules, Azure DevOps pipelines and AKS environments.
- Designed a hub-spoke network using Terraform, including Azure Firewall, private DNS zones, private endpoints for storage and SQL, and VNet peering across three subscriptions.
- Added Terratest module tests to the pipeline and implemented a nightly infrastructure drift-detection job.
- Replaced manual deployment processes for 15 internal .NET and Node applications with Azure DevOps YAML pipelines covering build, test and deployment to App Service or AKS.
- Increased deployment frequency from roughly monthly to several times per week for most applications.
- Operate AKS upgrades, node pools and ingress; application manifests are owned by development teams.

Freelance IT Support | 2022–2023
- Created a repeatable PowerShell script and checklist for small-business Microsoft 365 security baselines.
- Supported clients with enabling MFA, Conditional Access, mailbox auditing and backups.

Systems Administrator | Maasbrug Gemeente IT Services | 2014–2020
- Administered Windows and Linux servers and supported staff across municipal services.
- Led the planning and execution of a lift-and-shift migration of 60 VMware servers to Azure IaaS using Azure Migrate.
- Completed the cutover over six weekends with no unplanned downtime.
- Used Azure VMs, VNets, site-to-site VPN and PowerShell in the migration.
- Supported an environment of approximately 250 Windows and Linux servers.

Career Breaks and Professional Development

Full-time caregiving | March 2020–August 2022
- Took time away from paid work to care for his father full time.
- Kept Azure Administrator (AZ-104) knowledge current and provided unpaid IT help to church and family.

Professional development | February 2024–February 2025
- Completed a three-month, part-time, online English-language cloud bootcamp in December 2024.
- Studied Terraform and passed the Terraform Associate certification in 2025.
- Built a Proxmox homelab.

Certifications
- Microsoft Certified: Azure Administrator Associate (AZ-104)
- Terraform Associate, 2025

critique.content_quality_feedback: This is a strong, well-structured CV with clear section headings, relevant technical skills, quantified achievements, and credible project detail. The strongest evidence is the 60-server VMware-to-Azure migration completed over six weekends without unplanned downtime, the three-subscription hub-spoke design, and the improvement in deployment frequency from roughly monthly to several times per week. The career break is disclosed professionally and the document avoids unexplained employment gaps. Minor weaknesses are that some responsibilities are described as task lists rather than outcomes, the level of system-design responsibility is not explicit, and the overlap between the 2022–2023 freelance period and the March 2020–August 2022 caregiving period could be clarified through more precise dates. There are no apparent unsupported skills or experiences compared with the original candidate information.
critique.ats_compatibility_feedback: The CV is ATS-friendly: it uses conventional headings, simple text formatting, searchable technology names, and no problematic tables, graphics, or columns. It contains strong matches for Azure, Terraform, Azure DevOps, AKS, networking, security, Linux, Windows, VMware, and virtual machines. Its AI-screening probability is good for Azure-focused infrastructure/platform roles. Alignment would be weaker for this particular vacancy because the CV does not contain Terragrunt, mutual TLS, SSL/TLS, certificate management, AWS, IoT/remote-device integration, or explicit system-design and stakeholder-management terminology. These are candidate-profile gaps or unsupported areas, not formatting defects, so they should not be added without evidence.
critique.job_alignment_feedback: The document shows a strong match for hands-on infrastructure engineering, Azure cloud environment design and operation, Terraform, networking, practical security, Linux, and virtual machines. It also provides credible evidence of ownership through landing-zone work, AKS operations, infrastructure testing, drift detection, migration leadership, and deployment automation. Azure is an acceptable major-cloud background because the advertisement states that AWS is preferred but other major clouds are acceptable. The main alignment gaps are Terragrunt, mTLS/SSL/TLS and certificate management, IoT or remote-device integration, JVM/backend development, and explicit evidence of leading technical proposals while bringing stakeholders along. The CV also does not directly demonstrate the advertised train-to-cloud, telemetry, alerting, video-streaming, or remote-content-update domain. Its strongest positioning is as an Azure platform/infrastructure engineer with substantial migration, networking, IaC, CI/CD, and operations experience.
critique.improvement_instructions:
MINOR IMPROVEMENTS:
1. In the Professional Summary, make the systems-design and operational-ownership evidence more explicit without adding unsupported claims. For example, revise the opening to: "Cloud infrastructure engineer with experience designing, building and operating Azure environments, including landing zones, hub-spoke networking, infrastructure-as-code, CI/CD platforms and AKS operations." Retain the existing migration and deployment-frequency achievements.

2. In the Professional Experience section under Havenstad Logistics, revise the first two bullets so they show design ownership and operational scope more clearly. For example, change "Build and maintain Azure landing-zone infrastructure, Terraform modules, Azure DevOps pipelines and AKS environments" to "Design, build and operate Azure landing-zone infrastructure, Terraform modules, Azure DevOps pipelines and AKS environments." Keep the existing hub-spoke networking details immediately after it.

3. In the Havenstad Logistics section, clarify the collaboration boundary already supported by the source material. Change "application manifests are owned by development teams" to "Operate AKS upgrades, node pools and ingress while coordinating the application-manifest ownership boundary with development teams." Do not imply broader stakeholder leadership than the candidate has documented.

4. In the Technical Skills section, keep the existing supported networking and security terms but group them under a more searchable heading such as "Networking and security" and retain exact terms including "Azure Firewall," "private endpoints," "site-to-site VPN," "Entra ID," "MFA," "Conditional Access," and "Microsoft 365 security baseline." This improves retrieval of the candidate's practical security evidence without adding mTLS or SSL/TLS claims.

5. In the Career Breaks and Professional Development section, make the chronology easier to parse by using consistent month-year ranges. For example, present the freelance period as "2022–2023" only if exact months are unavailable, and state the professional-development period as "February 2024–February 2025." If the freelance work overlapped with caregiving, add a short truthful qualifier such as "part-time freelance work during this period" only if that accurately reflects the arrangement.

6. In the Professional Development subsection, remove the phrase "English-language" from "three-month, part-time, online English-language cloud bootcamp" unless language of instruction is relevant to the application. Replace it with the more concise supported wording: "Completed a three-month, part-time, online cloud bootcamp in December 2024."

critique.content_quality_feedback: This is a strong, well-structured CV with clear progression from systems administration into Azure cloud and platform engineering. The summary is targeted, the experience bullets are specific, and several achievements are quantified: a 60-server migration completed over six weekends with no unplanned downtime, 15 application pipelines, and deployment frequency increasing from roughly monthly to several times per week. The career break is handled transparently and professionally. The main content limitations are that stakeholder leadership, systems architecture, and security outcomes are not described as explicitly as the job requires. The overlap between Freelance IT Support (2022–2023) and full-time caregiving through August 2022 could also be clarified.
critique.ats_compatibility_feedback: The CV uses conventional headings, simple text formatting, standard reverse-chronological experience, and ATS-friendly keyword groupings. It contains strong matches for Azure, Terraform, Azure DevOps, AKS, networking, Linux, VMware, PowerShell, and security. AI screening probability is high for Azure-focused infrastructure/platform roles. Screening probability is lower for this particular vacancy because the document does not contain Terragrunt, mTLS, SSL/TLS, certificate management, or AWS terminology. Those are genuine experience gaps rather than keywords that should be added without supporting evidence. For maximum parsing consistency, use a conventional heading such as 'Professional Experience' consistently and avoid relying on slash-separated labels where a direct keyword can be used.
critique.job_alignment_feedback: The document aligns strongly with the hands-on infrastructure, Azure environment design and operation, Terraform, networking, security-awareness, Linux, and virtual-machine aspects of the role. The hub-spoke design, Azure Firewall, private endpoints, VPN, landing zones, Terraform modules, drift detection, and AKS operation are particularly relevant to a platform that must be reliable and secure. Azure is an acceptable major-cloud background even though AWS is preferred. The CV does not establish Terragrunt, mutual TLS, SSL/TLS, certificate management, IoT or remote-device integration, JVM/backend development, or direct experience agreeing interfaces with external manufacturers. It also shows technical ownership through the migration and infrastructure work, but does not clearly demonstrate leading technical proposals across stakeholders or bringing stakeholders along. These are alignment gaps, not defects that can be solved by unsupported wording.
critique.improvement_instructions:
MINOR/MEANINGFUL IMPROVEMENTS:
1. In the Professional Summary, replace the final sentence with a more role-aligned, evidence-based formulation such as: "Experienced in designing and operating Azure cloud infrastructure, improving platform reliability through Terraform testing and drift detection, and enabling more frequent internal application releases through automated build, test and deployment pipelines." This makes infrastructure operation, reliability, and deployment enablement more explicit without adding unsupported experience.
2. In the Cloud Engineer experience section under Havenstad Logistics, revise the first bullet to explicitly include the job's supported terminology: "Design and operate Azure cloud infrastructure, including Azure landing zones, Terraform modules, Azure DevOps pipelines and AKS environments." Only use this wording if "operate" accurately covers the stated responsibilities; the existing AKS upgrade, node-pool and ingress bullet supports it.
3. In the same Havenstad section, strengthen the hub-spoke networking bullet by starting with the design outcome: "Designed and implemented a hub-spoke Azure network across three subscriptions using Terraform, including Azure Firewall, private DNS zones, private endpoints for storage and SQL, and VNet peering." This makes systems/network design easier for both recruiters and ATS screening to identify.
4. In the same section, clarify the technical leadership evidence without overstating people or stakeholder management. For example, change the pipeline bullet to: "Replaced manual deployment processes for 15 internal .NET and Node applications by designing and implementing Azure DevOps YAML pipelines covering build, test and deployment to App Service or AKS." This demonstrates ownership of a technical topic from implementation through operational use.
5. In the Career Breaks and Professional Development section, clarify the date overlap by changing the Freelance IT Support dates to a month-level range if known, or add a short parenthetical such as "(including work undertaken before August 2022)" only if accurate. This prevents the 2022–2023 freelance period from appearing inconsistent with the March 2020–August 2022 caregiving period.
6. In the Technical Skills section, retain the existing accurate skills but consider changing "Cloud and infrastructure" to "Cloud infrastructure and environment design" and "Networking and security" to "Networking and security awareness." These labels better reflect the job's terminology while remaining supported by the documented Azure network, firewall, VPN, Microsoft 365 security, and identity work.

Do not add Terragrunt, mTLS, SSL/TLS, certificate management, AWS, IoT, automotive integration, JVM development, or external-manufacturer stakeholder management unless the candidate has that experience and can document it.
